children: The widely-expected 25 basis point jump in the official cash rate - the second in succession - came after inflation that hit 4.1% in the June quarter.
Policymakers said the latest rise would cut the risk of having to raise rates by a larger amount later and were dovish on the future path of rates.
“Future policy decisions will depend on the (Monetary Policy) Committee’s judgement of the balance of risks to medium-term inflation,” the central bank said.
“After lacklustre growth in the June quarter, New Zealand’s economic recovery has most likely resumed but remains uneven."
Reporting by Frank Prenesti for Sharecast.com
